To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

vector perturbation precoding suffers from a severe performance degradation if the channel state information is not perfect and that this can be overcome by a simple scheme that we term transmit outage vector perturbation precoder (TOP).
VP is not robust to the violation of its idealizing assumptions and that the proposed TOP scheme is a robust alternative to VP.
VP is a promising precoding technique, but that the performance of the scheme can be significantly improved by taking into account the imperfections of the practical system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of VP precoding and TOP for practical multiuser systems with limited CSI, limited transmit power normalization accuracy, and limited dynamic range.
the design and analysis of practical precoding schemes for multiuser MIMO systems.
the development and analysis of VP precoding schemes that are more robust to imperfect CSI and realistic assumptions on the receivers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VP is not a practical scheme, at least in its present form.
VP precoding should be applied only when the channel is perfectly known and when the receiver is equipped with an infinite dynamic range.
VP precoding is not robust to practical imperfections and that it is necessary to develop more sophisticated schemes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VP precoding is not a practical alternative to dirty paper coding.
VP precoding is a powerful tool but that it needs to be used with great care.
VP precoding is not as robust as it was previously believed to be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VP precoding is not robust and that the TOP scheme is a viable alternative.
the VP scheme as originally proposed in the literature is not robust against practical implementation issues.
